question: According to Section 12 of the Colorado CDL Manual, which set of exercises may be used to test an applicant's basic control skills, either off-road or on the street during the Road Test?
choice_a: Straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, parallel park (driver side), parallel park (conventional), and alley dock
choice_b: Forward stop, straight-line backing, forward offset tracking, and reverse offset backing
choice_c: Three-point turn, K-turn, and parallel park only
choice_d: Uphill start, downhill start, and emergency stop
explanation: Section 12 lists the exercises as straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, parallel park (driver side), parallel park (conventional), and alley dock, shown in Figures 12-1 through 12-6.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 126

question: What four categories does the examiner use to score the Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test under Section 12?
choice_a: Speed, smoothness, mirror use, and signal use
choice_b: Crossing boundaries (encroachments), pull-ups, outside vehicle observations (looks), and final position/inside parallel
choice_c: Time to complete, fuel efficiency, gear selection, and steering angle
choice_d: Number of stops, number of starts, engine RPM, and brake pressure
explanation: Section 12.1 Scoring lists crossing boundaries (encroachments), pull-ups, outside vehicle observations (looks), and final position/inside parallel as the four scored categories.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 126

question: How does the Colorado CDL Manual define an "encroachment" during the Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Any time the applicant stops the vehicle for more than five seconds
choice_b: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle
choice_c: Failing to use a turn signal before backing
choice_d: Exceeding the posted speed limit within the exercise area
explanation: The manual states the examiner scores encroachments as the number of times the applicant touches or crosses over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle, and each encroachment counts as an error.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 126

question: According to Section 12, what is the maximum number of times an applicant may look to check the position of the vehicle during most exercises, and which exercise is the exception?
choice_a: One look maximum for all exercises, no exceptions
choice_b: Two looks maximum, except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows only one look
choice_c: Three looks maximum for all exercises
choice_d: Unlimited looks are allowed on every exercise
explanation: The manual states the maximum number of looks is two, "except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows one look."
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 126-127

question: In the Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise described in Section 12, on which side is the parking space located, and what must the applicant achieve?
choice_a: On the right; the vehicle only needs its rear wheels inside the space
choice_b: On the left; the applicant must drive past the entrance, then back in without crossing front, side, or rear boundaries, getting the entire vehicle completely into the space
choice_c: On the left; cones may be touched as long as they are not knocked over
choice_d: Directly in front of the vehicle; no backing is required
explanation: The manual states the applicant may be asked to park in a space on the left, driving past the entrance parallel to the parking area, then backing in without crossing the boundaries, getting the entire vehicle completely into the space.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 127

question: In the Alley Dock exercise under Section 12, how close must the rear of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley, and what must be true of the vehicle's final position?
choice_a: Within one foot of the rear of the alley; the vehicle may be at any angle
choice_b: Within three feet of the rear of the alley; the vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane when the maneuver is completed
choice_c: Within ten feet of the rear of the alley; no straightness requirement applies
choice_d: The vehicle must touch the rear boundary line exactly
explanation: The manual states the applicant must back into the alley, bringing the rear of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones, and the vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane when completed.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, p. 127-128

question: According to Section 13, what three things must an applicant do at all times during the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Wear a safety belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_b: Keep both windows down, use hazard flashers continuously, and avoid all intersections
choice_c: Drive at the posted speed limit exactly, avoid highways, and use only the leftmost lane
choice_d: Avoid using turn signals, coast through turns, and keep one hand on the wheel
explanation: Section 13 states the applicant must drive in a safe and responsible manner, wear a safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 130

question: What does the manual say happens if the on-road test route does not include a particular traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing?
choice_a: The applicant automatically receives full credit for that maneuver
choice_b: The applicant may be asked to simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing
choice_c: The examiner reschedules the test to a different route
choice_d: That portion of the test is skipped entirely with no substitute
explanation: The manual states that if the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the applicant may be asked to simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing if in that situation.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 130

question: How does Section 13 define "unsafe coasting" as it relates to making a turn during the on-road test?
choice_a: Braking too gently before reaching the turn
choice_b: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_c: Signaling more than 100 feet before a turn
choice_d: Failing to downshift twice before a turn
explanation: The manual states unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 130

question: According to Section 13, what must NOT happen while a vehicle is driving through an intersection during the on-road test?
choice_a: The vehicle must not roll forward or backward, and the driver must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: The driver must not use turn signals inside the intersection
choice_c: The driver must not check mirrors while inside the intersection
choice_d: The driver must not accelerate until fully clear of the intersection by 500 feet
explanation: The manual instructs that the vehicle must not roll forward or backward when stopped at an intersection, and that the driver must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 130

question: In the Stop/Start maneuver under Section 13, what is the correct order of actions once the vehicle has come to a full stop off the road, before moving the gear shift to neutral or park?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake, then cancel the turn signal, then activate the four-way flashers
choice_b: Cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, then apply the parking brake
choice_c: Activate the four-way flashers, remove feet from the pedals, then apply the parking brake
choice_d: Sound the horn, then apply the parking brake, then cancel the turn signal
explanation: The manual's sequence once stopped is: cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and then move the gear shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 131

question: According to Section 13, what must a driver NOT do while any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_c: Continue checking mirrors and traffic
choice_d: Maintain a steady speed through the crossing
explanation: The manual states the driver must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 131

question: For a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards approaching a railroad crossing, what do Section 13's special procedures require regarding four-way flashers and the stopping distance from the nearest rail?
choice_a: Activate four-way flashers within 100 feet of the crossing; stop within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Activate four-way flashers within 200 feet of the crossing; stop the front of the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Activate four-way flashers within 500 feet of the crossing; stop within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: No flashers are required; simply stop at the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states these vehicles must activate the four-way flashers within 200 feet of the railroad crossing and stop the front of the vehicle within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet, from the nearest rail.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 131

question: During the school bus student discharge maneuver described in Section 13, how far away from the students must the bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 5 feet away
choice_b: At least 10 feet away
choice_c: At least 20 feet away
choice_d: At least 30 feet away
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 132

question: Under Section 13's general driving behavior guidance on brake usage, what should a driver avoid, and what technique should be used instead?
choice_a: Avoid riding or pumping the brake and avoid braking harshly; brake smoothly using steady pressure
choice_b: Avoid using the brake at all while descending a grade
choice_c: Avoid downshifting before applying the brake
choice_d: Avoid braking until the vehicle has fully stopped rolling
explanation: The manual instructs: do not ride or pump the brake, do not brake harshly, and brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 132

question: Under Section 12M, what four steps make up the current Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Parallel park, alley dock, straight backing, and offset backing
choice_b: Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_c: Uphill start, downhill start, lane change, and emergency stop
choice_d: Left turn, right turn, U-turn, and three-point turn
explanation: Section 12M lists the exercises as Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, shown in Figures 12M.1 through 12M.4.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 146

topic: Basic Control Skills Test (12M) - Looks and Unsafe Acts
question: Under Section 12M, what happens if an applicant opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park) during an exercise?
choice_a: It is simply scored as one "look" with no further consequence
choice_b: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_c: The examiner issues a warning and the applicant may retry the exercise
choice_d: It only counts against the applicant if it happens more than twice
explanation: The manual states that if the applicant opens the door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 146

topic: Basic Control Skills Test (12M) - Free Looks
question: Under Section 12M, how many free "looks" is an applicant allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), respectively?
choice_a: Zero free looks on either exercise
choice_b: One free look on Exercise 2, and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_c: Two free looks on Exercise 2, and one free look on Exercise 4
choice_d: Unlimited free looks on both exercises
explanation: The manual states the applicant may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 146

question: In Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) under Section 12M, what must the applicant do while driving forward through the alley, and how many times may they stop?
choice_a: Stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it; the applicant may stop only once
choice_b: Stop as many times as necessary to line up the vehicle correctly
choice_c: Back up if the vehicle overshoots the stop box
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously while approaching the stop box
explanation: The manual states the applicant must drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it, and may stop only once.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 147

question: In Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking) under Section 12M, how many free "back-ups" are allowed, and is the applicant permitted to exit the vehicle during the exercise?
choice_a: Two free back-ups are allowed, and the applicant may exit once
choice_b: There are no free back-ups, and the applicant is not permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise
choice_c: Unlimited free back-ups are allowed, but exiting is prohibited
choice_d: One free back-up is allowed, and exiting is unrestricted
explanation: The manual states there are no free back-ups on Exercise 3, and the applicant is not permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 148

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing) under Section 12M, how close must the rear most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley, and how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed?
choice_a: Within three feet of the rear of the alley; two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: Within one foot of the rear of the alley; one free pull-up and one exit
choice_c: Within ten feet of the rear of the alley; no free pull-ups or exits
choice_d: Within five feet of the rear of the alley; three free pull-ups and unlimited exits
explanation: The manual requires the applicant to offset back into the alley, bringing the rear most part of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley, and allows two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 148

topic: Basic Control Skills Test (12M) - Road Test
question: According to Section 12M, what must happen before an applicant can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: The applicant must complete only Exercise 4
choice_b: The Basic Control Skills Test must be passed
choice_c: The applicant must pass a written retest
choice_d: The examiner must waive all skills exercises
explanation: The manual states: "Remember, the Basic Control Skills Test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test."
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 149

topic: Basic Control Skills Test (12M) - Unsafe Act
question: Under Section 12M, what is given as an example of an "unsafe act" that may result in automatic failure of the Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Sounding the horn after completing an exercise
choice_b: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion
choice_c: Using a turn signal before starting a maneuver
choice_d: Checking mirrors before backing
explanation: The manual gives examples of unsafe acts, including "forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion," which may result in automatic failure and the test being terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12M - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 147

question: According to Section 13.1.7, what should a driver do before entering a curve?
choice_a: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_b: Reduce speed before entering the curve so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_c: Shift into neutral to coast through the curve
choice_d: Change lanes to get the best angle through the curve
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to reduce speed before entering the curve so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve, and to keep the vehicle in the lane.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-Road Driving, p. 131
